response.title: What else do I have to buy or set up with a wire-free robot mower, like an antenna pole, a little garage, or spare blades?
response.answer:
A wire-free robotic lawn mower usually needs more than just the mower, but you don't necessarily need to buy all the accessories manufacturers advertise.

The biggest factor is the mower's navigation technology. Some require an outdoor antenna or reference station, while others use cameras, LiDAR, or network-based positioning and need almost no extra hardware.

Useful for getting a clear sky view. Not every mower needs one.




Charging station

	

Essential

	

Usually included. Needs an accessible outdoor power source.




Outdoor electrical outlet

	

Essential

	

May require installation if there isn't one nearby.




Robot mower garage

	

Optional

	

Protects against sun and rain; must be compatible with the mower.




Spare cutting blades

	

Recommended

	

Consumable parts worth keeping on hand.




Replacement battery

	

Not initially needed

	

Usually lasts multiple seasons, depending on use.




Wi-Fi extender or cellular service

	

Sometimes

	

Depends on how the mower receives updates, commands, and corrections.




Boundary markers or magnetic tags

	

Model-dependent

	

Some wire-free systems use markers for difficult areas or navigation.




Cleaning brush and maintenance tools

	

Recommended

	

Helpful for removing grass buildup and debris.

What I'd actually buy first

Check the included equipment. Many packages already contain the charging dock, RTK antenna, mounting hardware, and starter blades.

Solve the power and antenna placement. These are the most important installation issues. RTK reference stations need an unobstructed sky view and a rigid mount. 
Husqvarna US

Keep one compatible replacement blade set. There's no need to stockpile blades initially.

Wait on the garage. First verify that the mower can reliably navigate into its dock. A garage can interfere with satellite reception or docking on some models.

Check recurring costs. Some models use cellular connectivity or correction services that may involve subscriptions.

For a typical installation, I'd reserve roughly $50–$200 for initial accessories, excluding any new electrical outlet or an expensive manufacturer-specific garage. You may spend considerably less if the mower includes everything.

One important detail: wire-free means no buried perimeter wire, not necessarily no cables at all. The dock and sometimes the RTK antenna still need power.
